raw_response:
I will not spread my 12.4 mu too thin, but I also will not put everything into one crop. I have done this land for 30 years, so I start from what worked last year and only adjust a little. Around Quzhou, if cotton is managed well and I can irrigate from the well, it still makes sense to keep cotton as the main crop, but I do not want all my money tied up there because cotton needs more sprays and more watching. Maize is steady, wheat keeps grain in hand, peanut and mung bean help me spread risk and cash flow. I have middle school education, so I do look at fertilizer balance, but I still farm by what I saw work nearby. If neighbors got a good stand and better yield from improved or hybrid seed, I will use that. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing yield is worse, so I will not cut too hard. I will keep phosphorus under the seed or in the base, nitrogen split where needed, and I will use the well when the crop is really asking for water instead of waiting for the sky.

For cotton, I will keep the better ground and more attention on it, with enough nitrogen and potash because weak cotton later in the season costs me more than a few extra kilos of fertilizer. Wheat and maize I will run in a more standard way, close to what people around me do, because those are the crops where being too clever usually does not pay. Peanut I will keep on lighter land with decent base fertilizer and not too much nitrogen, otherwise vines run and pods do not fill right. Mung bean I will keep as the low-input crop: not much fertilizer, not much water, just enough to make it worth planting. Since some family members work off-farm, I also have to think about labor. That means I will not choose plans that need too many hand operations unless the crop can pay for it.

I will split the rest across wheat, maize, peanut, and mung bean so I have steady grain, some cash crops, and less risk if one crop fails. I will mostly follow what worked last year and what good farmers around me are doing, using improved or hybrid seed where I have seen better results.
